Carbon Trust (2011). Micro-CHP Accelerator: Final report. CTC788. Carbon Trust, London, March 2011.

UK field trial (2005-2008) of 87 micro-CHP units (72 domestic Stirling engines of 1-3 kWe peak (8-15 kWth), 15 small-commercial IC engines of 5-10 kWe / 12-25 kWth: Baxi Dachs, EC Power XRGI 13, Frichs 22, Fiat Totem) against 36 condensing boilers. Out of scope: buildings scale; units far smaller than the reciprocating-engine_chp archetype (industrial MW scale, ~40% electrical) and no Stirling archetype exists, so not extracted. Numbers it has: domestic Stirling annual thermal 71%, electrical 6%, H:P about 12:1, marginal cost over a condensing boiler about GBP 2,500 (retail GBP 5,000 vs boiler GBP 2,500 installed); small-commercial IC engine mean thermal 52.0%, electrical 22.3% (net), H:P about 2.3, about 6,000 h/yr (CF ~68%), gas 1.923 kWh per kWh heat, carbon 0.129 kgCO2/kWh heat (45% below a condensing boiler, range 33-57%); condensing boilers measured mean annual efficiency 85% (domestic; 85.5% thermal and -1.5% electrical assumed for comparison). Indicative installed small-commercial prices (Fig. 5.6): 5 kWe GBP 17,000, 13 kWe GBP 50,000 (2011, installed and commissioned; payback 20-23 years). Fuel cells not trialled. Answers no to-get row.
